questions.q: The National Testing Agency (NTA) is mainly responsible for:
options: conducting entrance examinations for higher education
questions.exp: NTA conducts exams such as JEE Main and NEET.

questions.q: The school structure proposed in NEP 2020 is:
questions.exp: The 5+3+3+4 design replaces the earlier 10+2 structure.

questions.q: NEP 2020 proposes that the minimum degree qualification for teaching will be:
questions.exp: By 2030 the 4-year integrated B.Ed. is to become the minimum qualification.

questions.q: Which of the following is a safe lab practice that a CS teacher should teach?
options: Shutting down systems properly and not eating near computers
Removing the power cable to shut down
questions.exp: Proper handling protects equipment and data.

questions.q: 'Assessment for learning' differs from 'assessment of learning' in that it:
options: is used to guide and improve instruction during learning
is conducted only at the end
questions.exp: Assessment for learning is formative, whereas assessment of learning is summative.

questions.q: A CS teacher giving students of different levels tasks of varying difficulty on the same topic is practising:
questions.exp: Tasks are adapted to readiness levels.

questions.q: According to NEP 2020, the secondary stage covers the ages of:
questions.exp: The secondary stage consists of Grades 9 to 12.

questions.q: Construct validity indicates how well a test measures:
options: a theoretical trait such as intelligence or creativity
questions.exp: It checks whether the test measures the abstract construct it claims to.

questions.q: Reflective teaching involves:
options: thinking critically about one's own teaching to improve it
questions.exp: Reflective practice, associated with Schon, uses experience as a basis for improvement.

questions.q: A rating scale is useful for evaluating:
options: qualities such as attitudes and performance on a continuum
questions.exp: Rating scales record the degree of a trait, for example from excellent to poor.

questions.q: An epidiascope is used to:
options: project opaque objects such as pictures from books
questions.exp: The epidiascope can project both opaque pictures and transparencies.

questions.q:
Statement I: Teaching algorithms before coding helps students to separate logic from syntax.
Statement II: Students should be told to memorise code rather than understand it.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statements I and II are true
Both Statements I and II are false
questions.exp: Understanding logic matters more than memorising code.

questions.q: In Maslow's hierarchy of needs, which need must be satisfied first for a child to be ready to learn?
options: Physiological needs such as food and rest
questions.exp: Lower-level needs like hunger and sleep take priority before higher needs can motivate learning.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of NEP 2020 regarding board examinations?
options: Making them low-stakes with an emphasis on testing core concepts and skills
Conducting them only once at the end of Grade 12 with memory focus
questions.exp: Board exams are to be redesigned to reduce pressure and test competencies.

questions.q: In education, action research was popularised by:
questions.exp: Corey applied action research to improve school practices.

questions.q: Which body is responsible for developing the National Curriculum Framework and model textbooks?
questions.exp: NCERT prepares the NCF and model textbooks for schools.

questions.q: Before writing a program in a class, a teacher should first ask students to:
questions.exp: Planning the logic first improves problem-solving.

questions.q: According to Dewey, the first step in the problem-solving method is:
questions.exp: Dewey's steps begin with recognising a felt difficulty, then defining it, hypothesising, testing and concluding.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best aid to show a trend in marks over several years?
questions.exp: A line graph shows change over time clearly.

questions.q: A unit plan differs from a lesson plan because it:
options: is meant for a single period only
covers a larger part of the syllabus spread over several periods
questions.exp: A unit plan organises a whole unit while a lesson plan covers one period.

questions.q: A recorded video lecture that a student can watch at any time is an example of:
questions.exp: The learner can access it at a time of choice.

questions.q: Brainstorming is a technique in which:
options: only the best idea is allowed
the teacher judges every idea at once
many ideas are generated freely without immediate criticism
answers are copied from the textbook
questions.exp: Osborn's brainstorming defers judgement to encourage a large number of creative ideas.

questions.q: Which is the correct sequence of the maxims 'known to unknown' used for teaching a new CS topic?
options: Start with the most advanced topic and go backward
Link the new topic to what students already know and then extend it
Begin with the unknown and then revise the known
questions.exp: Using prior knowledge as the starting point is the 'known to unknown' maxim.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of intrinsic motivation in a classroom?
options: A student studies to win a cash prize
A student studies to avoid punishment
A student studies to please the examiner
A student solves puzzles because she enjoys the challenge
questions.exp: Intrinsic motivation comes from interest and enjoyment of the activity itself, not external rewards.

questions.q: The principle of community-centredness suggests that the curriculum should:
options: be made only for the urban area
reflect the social and cultural needs of the community
questions.exp: The school serves society, so content should relate to community life.

questions.q: Objective-type tests are called objective because:
options: scoring does not depend on the examiner's personal judgement
questions.exp: The answer key is fixed, so any scorer gives the same marks.

questions.q: Selection-type items include:
questions.exp: In selection items the answer is selected from the options given.

questions.q: Enrichment programmes are designed mainly for:
questions.exp: Enrichment adds depth and challenge for talented children.

questions.q: Which of the following is an unethical practice for a teacher?
options: Favouring some students in marking because of personal relations
questions.exp: Partiality violates fairness.

questions.q: SWAYAM is:
options: a social media site only for teachers
a national platform that offers free online courses (MOOCs) to learners in India
questions.exp: SWAYAM is the Government of India MOOC platform from the Ministry of Education.

questions.q: Learning is best defined as:
options: a change caused only by growth and maturation
a change caused by fatigue or drugs
a relatively permanent change in behaviour brought about by experience or practice
questions.exp: Maturation, fatigue and drugs produce temporary or non-learned changes, so they are excluded from the definition.

questions.q: NEP 2020 supports a three-language formula which:
options: remains flexible and no language is imposed on any state
questions.exp: States, regions and students choose the languages, with at least two being Indian languages.

questions.q: Remedial teaching is given to:
options: students having specific learning difficulties identified through diagnosis
every student at the same time without need
questions.exp: It is corrective instruction targeted at diagnosed difficulties.

questions.q: Varying voice, gestures, movement and using pauses are components of the skill of:
questions.exp: Stimulus variation sustains attention by changing the stimuli presented to learners.

questions.q: Operant conditioning theory of learning is associated with:
questions.exp: Skinner studied how behaviour is shaped by reinforcement; Pavlov proposed classical conditioning.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a teaching skill in microteaching?
questions.exp: Budget preparation is an administrative task, not a classroom teaching skill.

questions.q: Professional development of a teacher is best promoted by:
options: attending workshops, reading and reflecting on one's teaching
questions.exp: Continuous learning keeps teaching effective.

questions.q: A well-designed blueprint helps mainly to improve:
questions.exp: It ensures that the test samples all the objectives and content areas.

questions.q: In Pavlov's experiment, the sound of the bell that initially caused no salivation is called the:
options: neutral stimulus which later becomes the conditioned stimulus
questions.exp: The bell was neutral at first; after pairing with food it became the conditioned stimulus.

questions.q: The skill of 'set induction' refers to:
options: summarising at the end of a lesson
creating readiness among students at the start of a lesson
questions.exp: Set induction prepares learners mentally for the new topic.

questions.q: A test that measures what a student has learnt after instruction in a subject is called:
questions.exp: Achievement tests measure acquired knowledge and skills.

questions.q: A questionnaire is a tool used to:
options: collect information in written form from respondents
questions.exp: It consists of a set of written questions for respondents.

questions.q: DIKSHA is:
options: a national digital platform for school education e-content
questions.exp: DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) provides e-content, QR-coded textbooks and teacher training.

questions.q: A spiral curriculum, proposed by Bruner, means that:
options: each topic is taught only once
topics are removed after the first class
topics are revisited at increasing levels of complexity
questions.exp: Concepts are repeatedly met at greater depth as learners grow.

questions.q: According to John Adams, teaching is a bipolar process. The two poles are:
questions.exp: Adams viewed teaching as a face-to-face interaction between the teacher and the learner.

questions.q: A hypothesis is best defined as:
options: a tentative statement about the relation between variables, to be tested
questions.exp: It is a testable proposition that guides the investigation.

questions.q: An activity-centred curriculum primarily emphasises:
questions.exp: Learning is organised around the activities of the learner.

questions.q: A collection of a student's work over time that shows progress is called:
questions.exp: Portfolio assessment documents learner growth through samples of work.

questions.q: A sociometric technique is used to find out:
options: the social relationships and acceptance among students in a group
questions.exp: Sociometry, developed by Moreno, shows preferences and rejections within a group.

questions.q: Norms of a standardised test are used to:
options: interpret an individual's score in comparison with a reference group
questions.exp: Norms give meaning to raw scores.

questions.q: A weighing scale always shows 2 kg more than the actual weight. The scale is:
questions.exp: It is consistent (reliable) but does not give the true weight (not valid).

questions.q: In the modern view, the teacher's role is best described as:
questions.exp: The teacher guides and supports learners in constructing knowledge.

questions.q: The test-retest method estimates reliability by:
options: giving two different tests to different groups
giving the same test twice to the same group and correlating the scores
checking the paper twice by one teacher
questions.exp: The correlation between two administrations shows stability.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Microteaching reduces the complexity of normal teaching.
Reason (R): It limits the class size, time and number of skills practised.
Choose the correct option.
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Reducing size, time and skills makes the teaching situation simpler.

questions.q: Teachers' Day in India is celebrated on:
questions.exp: It marks the birth anniversary of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.

questions.q: The 'Holistic Progress Card' proposed in NEP 2020 will:
options: show only the marks of the final exam
give a 360-degree view of the learner's progress including self- and peer-assessment
questions.exp: It records cognitive, affective and psychomotor development.

questions.q: According to Piaget, children aged about 7 to 11 years are in the:
questions.exp: Logical thinking about concrete objects, conservation and classification develop in the concrete operational stage.

questions.q: Which of the following is a supply-type (recall) item?
questions.exp: Supply-type items require the student to produce the answer.

questions.q: A blueprint of a question paper is a:
options: three-dimensional chart showing weightage to objectives, content and question forms
questions.exp: The blueprint ensures balanced coverage of objectives, content and types of questions.

questions.q: NEP 2020 recommended renaming the Ministry of Human Resource Development as:
questions.exp: The ministry was renamed accordingly.

questions.q:
Statement I: Objective-type questions can cover a large amount of content in a short time.
Statement II: Objective-type questions are best to test the writing skill of students.
Choose the correct option.
questions.exp: Objective items sample wide content but do not test writing ability.

questions.q: A curriculum that arranges learning around subjects like Physics, History and Computer Science is called:
questions.exp: A subject-centred curriculum organises knowledge by disciplines.

questions.q:
Statement I: NEP 2020 promotes multidisciplinary education without rigid separation of arts and sciences.
Statement II: NEP 2020 proposes rigid streams that students cannot cross after Grade 10.
Choose the correct option.
questions.exp: NEP 2020 removes hard separations between streams.

questions.q: A teacher-made test is different from a standardised test because the teacher-made test:
options: is prepared by the teacher for a specific class and lacks established norms
is administered to the whole country
questions.exp: Standardised tests have tried-out items, norms and uniform procedures.

questions.q: In the teaching of CS, a practical examination along with a viva voce is useful as it:
options: tests skills and understanding that written tests cannot
questions.exp: Hands-on tasks and oral questioning show real competence.

questions.q: General objectives differ from specific objectives in that general objectives are:
options: broad aims of teaching a subject, and specific ones are what a lesson achieves
questions.exp: General objectives are broad; specific objectives are lesson-level and measurable.

questions.q: NEP 2020 replaced which earlier national policy on education?
questions.exp: NEP 2020 is the first education policy of the 21st century, succeeding the 1986 policy.

questions.q:
Statement I: A teacher should keep updating subject knowledge.
Statement II: Once a teacher gets a degree, there is no need for further learning.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statements I and II are true
Both Statements I and II are false
questions.exp: Knowledge changes fast, so a teacher must keep learning.

questions.q: The project method of teaching was popularised by:
questions.exp: Kilpatrick developed the project method on the basis of John Dewey's philosophy.

questions.q: In the inductive method of teaching:
options: examples are studied first and then a general rule is derived
a rule is stated first and then applied to examples
there is no use of examples
questions.exp: Induction proceeds from particular instances to a general principle.

questions.q: An open-book examination primarily tests:
options: application and understanding rather than rote memorisation
questions.exp: With resources available, questions focus on higher-order skills.

questions.q: Summative assessment is mainly used to:
options: judge the overall achievement at the end of a course
questions.exp: It is used for grading, certification and promotion.

questions.q: Which is the correct cycle of action research?
questions.exp: The cycle repeats with the revised plan after reflection.

questions.q: The historical method of research is concerned with:
options: studying past events using records and documents
questions.exp: It involves critical examination of sources.

questions.q: In the role-play method, learners:
options: listen to the teacher's continuous talk
act out situations or characters to understand a concept or problem
questions.exp: Role play develops empathy, communication and understanding through enactment.

questions.q: Fluency in questioning means:
options: asking questions smoothly and in a logical sequence
asking the same question again and again
questions.exp: Fluency means the ability to frame and ask questions without hesitation.

questions.q: After a first microteaching session, the trainee should:
options: modify the lesson using the feedback and teach it again
give a test to the pupils
questions.exp: Re-plan and re-teach follow feedback in the cycle.

questions.q: A sample should be:
questions.exp: Representativeness allows generalisation to the population.

questions.q: Feedback in microteaching can be obtained from:
options: supervisor, peers and video or audio recordings
questions.exp: Multiple sources give objective information about the performance.

questions.q: In the jigsaw technique of cooperative learning:
options: each group member becomes an expert on one part and teaches it to the others
all students read the entire text alone
the teacher teaches each part in turn
students compete against each other for marks
questions.exp: Jigsaw makes learners interdependent as each one is responsible for teaching a part.

questions.q: Gender-sensitive teaching means that the teacher:
options: prefers boys in computer lab work
gives equal opportunity and respect to boys and girls
questions.exp: It avoids bias and promotes equity.

questions.q: The test–retest method is used to estimate which characteristic of a test?
questions.exp: Administering the same test twice and correlating scores gives the coefficient of stability (reliability).

questions.q: The maxim 'from concrete to abstract' in teaching means that a teacher should:
options: begin with definitions and later show examples
begin with real objects or examples before introducing ideas and symbols
teach only the abstract part of every topic
avoid examples when the topic is difficult
questions.exp: Learners grasp ideas more easily when they first see or handle concrete things.

questions.q: A student's marks are compared with other students' marks in:
questions.exp: Norm-referenced tests rank students relative to a group.

questions.q: PARAKH, proposed in NEP 2020, is:
options: a national assessment centre setting norms for student assessment
questions.exp: PARAKH stands for Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development.

questions.q: The heuristic method of teaching was advocated by:
questions.exp: Armstrong wanted students to discover facts for themselves, as 'heurisko' means 'I find out'.

questions.q: A teacher's cooperation with parents is important because:
options: it supports the child's learning and behaviour at home and school
it reduces the teacher's work to nil
questions.exp: Joint effort improves the child's progress.

questions.q: A teacher finds that many students fail to complete programming exercises and tries a pair-programming strategy to check if results improve. This is an example of:
questions.exp: It is a systematic classroom study to solve a local problem.

questions.q: Project-based learning in CS, such as building a small library management program, helps to:
options: integrate concepts and develop real-world skills
questions.exp: Projects apply many concepts together.

questions.q: A student has mental age 12 and chronological age 10. The intelligence quotient is:
Pair programming in the classroom is an approach where:
options: two students work together at one computer, one coding and the other reviewing
each student works with different tasks silently
questions.exp: It promotes collaboration and fewer errors.

questions.q: In microteaching, the number of pupils generally taken is:
questions.exp: Small groups of about 5-10 pupils are used.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common misconception of novice programmers?
options: Understanding that assignment overwrites the old value
Believing that a variable stores all values it has ever held
questions.exp: A variable holds only its current value; novices often think it keeps history.

questions.q: The term 'null curriculum' refers to:
options: what the school does not teach but could have
questions.exp: Eisner used it for content and skills that are left out.

questions.q: Virtual labs help students by:
options: allowing them to perform simulated experiments online
questions.exp: They give access to experiments where physical labs are limited.

questions.q: Which of the following is a difference between curriculum and syllabus?
options: Syllabus is narrower and lists topics for a subject, while curriculum includes all learning experiences
questions.exp: Curriculum is broader and includes co-curricular experiences and methods.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A test can be reliable without being valid.
Reason (R): Reliability only ensures consistency, not that the right trait is measured.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Consistent measurement of the wrong thing is reliable but invalid.

questions.q: Dysgraphia is a disorder related to:
questions.exp: Dysgraphia affects handwriting and written expression.

questions.q: Correlation among subjects in a curriculum ensures that:
options: the number of subjects is doubled
related ideas in different subjects reinforce one another
questions.exp: Correlation links subjects so that learning is more meaningful.

questions.q: NEP 2020 recommends introducing coding to students from:
questions.exp: A fun course on coding starts in Grade 6 as part of computational thinking.

questions.q: The full form of MOOC is:
questions.exp: MOOCs are open-access online courses for large-scale participation.

questions.q: The validity of a test refers to:
options: the extent to which it measures what it is meant to measure
questions.exp: A valid test measures the intended attribute.

questions.q:
Statement I: Remedial teaching should follow a diagnostic procedure.
Statement II: Remedial teaching can be given without knowing the cause of the difficulty.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statements I and II are true
Both Statements I and II are false
questions.exp: Without diagnosis, the remedy may not address the real cause.

questions.q: Co-curricular activities such as debates and sports are included in the curriculum to:
options: develop the all-round personality of learners
questions.exp: They support social, emotional and physical development.

questions.q: NPTEL provides:
options: video and web courses in engineering and science through IITs and IISc
questions.exp: NPTEL is a joint initiative of the IITs and IISc.

questions.q: A teacher using private tuition to pressurise his own class students to join is an example of:
options: conflict of interest violating professional ethics
questions.exp: Using one's position for private gain is unethical.

questions.q: A rubric is:
options: a scoring guide listing criteria and performance levels
questions.exp: Rubrics make scoring of projects and essays transparent and consistent.

questions.q: e-PG Pathshala provides:
questions.exp: It is a UGC-MHRD initiative for e-content at the postgraduate level.

questions.q: Which principle of teaching is followed when a teacher first teaches addition and later multiplication?
questions.exp: Progressing from simple ideas to complex ones is the 'simple to complex' maxim.

questions.q: Who is credited, along with Allen, with the development of the microteaching technique at Stanford?
questions.exp: Dwight Allen and Robert Bush developed microteaching at Stanford University.

questions.q: The 'Pygmalion effect' in classrooms means that:
options: high teacher expectations tend to raise student performance
questions.exp: Rosenthal and Jacobson showed expectations influence achievement.

questions.q:
Statement I: ICT can help provide access to education in remote areas.
Statement II: ICT in education requires no training for teachers.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statements I and II are true
Both Statements I and II are false
questions.exp: ICT widens access, but teachers need training to use it effectively.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of effective teaching?
options: One-way flow of information with no learner participation
questions.exp: Effective teaching is interactive; one-way talk without participation is not.

questions.q: The research method in which the investigator collects data from a large group through questionnaires or interviews is the:
questions.exp: Survey research describes the existing conditions in a population.

questions.q: A democratic teacher in the classroom:
options: encourages participation and respects students' opinions
questions.exp: A democratic style promotes participation and responsibility.

questions.q: 'Unplugged' activities in computer science teaching are:
options: activities done only on the internet
activities that teach computing concepts without using computers
questions.exp: Examples include sorting with cards or searching games.

questions.q: The main purpose of action research in a classroom is to:
options: solve an immediate practical problem and improve practice
questions.exp: Action research is aimed at local, practical improvement.

questions.q: The 'Skill of illustrating with examples' is best shown when a teacher:
options: uses simple, relevant examples to clarify a rule
questions.exp: Relevant examples link abstract concepts to the learner's experience.

questions.q: The word 'curriculum' is derived from the Latin word 'currere', which means:
options: to run a race or course
questions.exp: Curriculum originally meant a race course or track to be run.

questions.q: Which of the following is a proper principle of remedial teaching?
options: It should be a repetition of the same method that failed
It should be individualised and encouraging
It should be done only by the principal
questions.exp: Different, supportive strategies suit the learner's difficulty.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a desirable quality of a teacher?
questions.exp: Teachers must be open to new ideas.

questions.q: Which is the correct sequence of the microteaching cycle?
questions.exp: The cycle is repeated until the skill is mastered.

questions.q: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act came into force in:
questions.exp: The RTE Act was passed in 2009 and came into force on 1 April 2010.

questions.q: Encouraging girls and students from rural backgrounds in CS classes is an example of:
options: equity and inclusion in computing education
questions.exp: Equal opportunities widen participation in computing.

questions.q: Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE) was mandated for elementary education under:
questions.exp: Section 29 of the RTE Act, 2009 provides for CCE.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-projected visual aid?
questions.exp: Charts, models and maps are shown directly without projection.

questions.q: The 5E instructional model consists of Engage, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate and:
questions.exp: The sequence is Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate.

questions.q: Digital citizenship education includes teaching students about:
options: responsible and ethical use of technology, privacy and netiquette
questions.exp: It prepares learners for safe and ethical use of ICT.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best specific objective for a computer science lesson?
options: The teacher will explain number systems
The student will convert the decimal number 25 into binary correctly
The student will know everything about numbers
questions.exp: It is specific, observable and measurable.

questions.q: Which method gives individual attention to students in small groups to clear their doubts after the main lecture?
questions.exp: A tutorial is a small-group or one-to-one session for clarifying difficulties and guided practice.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important criterion for selecting a teaching aid?
questions.exp: An aid must help achieve the specific objective of the lesson.

questions.q: A diagnostic test differs from an achievement test because it:
options: has many small items on specific skills to locate weak points
is conducted only at the end of the year
questions.exp: It analyses specific skills rather than giving an overall measure.

questions.q: An overhead projector (OHP) is classified as a:
questions.exp: OHP projects transparencies on a screen so it is a projected visual aid.

questions.q: Blended learning is:
options: a combination of face-to-face teaching and online learning
learning without a teacher or books
questions.exp: It combines classroom and online modes.

questions.q:
Match the method with its proponent:
P. Project method
Q. Heuristic method
R. Dalton Plan
S. Kindergarten system
questions.exp: Kilpatrick - project; Armstrong - heuristic; Parkhurst - Dalton; Froebel - kindergarten.

questions.q: Anecdotal record is a tool used to:
options: note the significant behaviour incidents of a student
questions.exp: It is a brief factual record of a particular observed event.

questions.q: The recapitulation questions asked at the end of a lesson serve to:
options: evaluate how far the objectives have been achieved
questions.exp: They check understanding and give feedback.

questions.q: Which of the following is a purely audio aid?
questions.exp: Radio gives only sound; film combines sound and picture.

questions.q: A cumulative record card is maintained to:
options: give rank in the class only
record the overall progress of a student over the years
questions.exp: It stores academic, personal and social information of the student.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of evaluation?
questions.exp: Evaluation aims at feedback, improvement and decision making.

questions.q: Skinner's operant conditioning is mainly concerned with:
questions.exp: Operant conditioning shapes voluntary behaviour by its consequences (reinforcement/punishment).

questions.q: NEP 2020 recommends that, wherever possible, the medium of instruction till at least Grade 5 should be:
options: the home language, mother tongue or local language
questions.exp: Children learn most easily in their home language.

questions.q:
Statement I: The hidden curriculum is part of the officially written syllabus.
Statement II: The hidden curriculum can influence the values of students.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statements I and II are true
Both Statements I and II are false
questions.exp: The hidden curriculum is unwritten, yet shapes values and attitudes.

questions.q: In criterion-referenced assessment, a student's performance is compared with:
questions.exp: The student is judged on whether the pre-set criterion has been achieved.

questions.q: An aptitude test is used to:
options: predict future ability to learn or perform in an area
questions.exp: Aptitude tests measure potential.

questions.q: The report 'Learning Without Burden' (1993) was chaired by:
questions.exp: The Yash Pal Committee highlighted the need to reduce curriculum load.

questions.q: Concurrent validity is checked by:
options: comparing with results after five years
comparing test scores with another established measure taken at about the same time
questions.exp: Concurrent validity uses a criterion available at present.

questions.q: Microteaching was first developed at:
questions.exp: Dwight Allen and colleagues developed it at Stanford in the early 1960s.

questions.q: A student with an IQ of about 140 is generally classified as:
questions.exp: IQ above about 130 is generally regarded as gifted.

questions.q: The dependent variable in an experiment on the effect of a new teaching method on marks is:
questions.exp: Marks depend on the method.

questions.q: In Morris Hunt's classification, which level of teaching is the highest?
questions.exp: Memory is the lowest, understanding is the middle and reflective level (problem-centred, critical thinking) is the highest.

questions.q: Evaluation is different from measurement because evaluation:
options: includes value judgement about the quantitative and qualitative evidence
questions.exp: Measurement gives numbers; evaluation interprets them against objectives.

questions.q: Microteaching is mainly used in:
questions.exp: It helps trainees and serving teachers develop specific skills.

questions.q: In an experimental study, the variable manipulated by the researcher is the:
questions.exp: The effect of the independent variable on the dependent variable is studied.

questions.q: Dry-running (tracing) a program on paper helps students to:
options: understand how values change step by step
questions.exp: Tracing builds an accurate mental model of execution.

questions.q: A teacher asks students to think of reasons why a program may be slow and to suggest improvements. This question mainly develops:
questions.exp: Analysing causes and proposing solutions is a higher-order thinking task.

questions.q: An underachiever is a student who:
options: performs below the level expected from his or her ability
questions.exp: Underachievement is a gap between potential and performance.

questions.q: Which of the following is a co-scholastic area?
questions.exp: Co-scholastic areas include life skills, attitudes, values, sports and arts.

questions.q: The mean of the scores 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 is:
OER stands for:
questions.exp: OER are freely available teaching and learning materials.

questions.q: Testing the previous knowledge of students at the start of a lesson is part of which step?
questions.exp: Previous knowledge is tested to link the new matter with what is already known.

questions.q: The annual plan of a teacher is prepared:
options: at the beginning of the academic session
questions.exp: It distributes the syllabus over the year.

questions.q: In Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience, the base of the cone (most concrete) is:
questions.exp: Dale placed direct experience at the bottom and verbal symbols at the top.

questions.q: The National Educational Technology Forum (NETF) was proposed in the NEP 2020 to:
options: provide a platform for free exchange of ideas on the use of technology for learning
questions.exp: NETF is an autonomous body for technology in education.

questions.q: ADHD is mainly characterised by:
questions.exp: Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder shows persistent inattention with hyperactivity/impulsivity.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of a lesson plan?
options: It removes the need for the teacher to know the subject
questions.exp: A lesson plan guides the teacher but cannot replace subject knowledge.

questions.q: Case study as a tool in remedial work helps the teacher to:
options: study an individual learner's background in depth
questions.exp: A case study gathers detailed information about one learner.

questions.q: Peer tutoring can help remedial work because:
options: students learn from classmates who explain things in simple language
questions.exp: Peers can provide additional support and explanation.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of error analysis in a programming class?
options: Examining students' wrong programs to find recurring misconceptions
questions.exp: Error analysis reveals the pattern of mistakes and their causes.

questions.q: The final stage of a research study is generally:
questions.exp: Findings are communicated through a report.

questions.q: Face validity means that:
options: the test appears on the surface to measure what it should
questions.exp: It is a superficial judgement of appropriateness.

questions.q: In CCE, the word 'comprehensive' means that the evaluation covers:
options: only the subjects in the examination
both scholastic and co-scholastic aspects of the learner's development
questions.exp: Comprehensive evaluation assesses overall development, including attitudes and skills.

questions.q:
Statement I: Action research begins with identifying a problem in one's own practice.
Statement II: Action research is conducted only by external experts.
Choose the correct option.
questions.exp: The teacher-practitioner identifies and investigates the problem.

questions.q: Which of the following is a principle of curriculum construction?
questions.exp: A good curriculum considers the needs and interests of the learner.

questions.q: In item analysis, the upper group had 18 correct answers and the lower group had 6 correct answers, each group having 20 students. The discrimination index is:
In a constructivist lesson plan, the teacher's main role is to:
options: arrange activities that help students build their own understanding
questions.exp: Constructivist plans centre on learner activity and guidance.

questions.q: NEP 2020 recommends public investment in education of:
questions.exp: The policy reiterates the target of 6% of GDP.

questions.q: Which skill uses simple examples, analogies and a clear sequence to make a concept understandable?
questions.exp: Explaining involves clear, connected statements with examples and links.

questions.q: A major limitation of essay-type questions is:
options: they cannot test organisation of ideas
questions.exp: Different examiners may give different marks to the same answer.

questions.q: Explaining a stack using a pile of plates is an example of using:
questions.exp: An analogy relates an unfamiliar concept to a familiar one.

questions.q: Constructivism holds that:
options: knowledge is poured into passive learners
learning is only memorisation of facts
learners actively build their own knowledge from experience
the teacher is the sole source of knowledge
questions.exp: Constructivists see learning as active construction of meaning on the basis of prior knowledge.

questions.q: Asking follow-up questions to push a student to give a complete or deeper answer is the skill of:
questions.exp: Probing prompts students to clarify, extend or justify their responses.

questions.q: A seminar is best described as:
options: a one-way lecture by an expert
a group meeting where papers are presented and discussed under guidance
a written test with objective questions
a practical session in the laboratory
questions.exp: In a seminar participants present prepared papers followed by interaction.

questions.q: SCERT stands for:
options: Standard Council for Education and Research Teaching
School Council of Examination and Reform Training
State Council of Educational Research and Training
State Centre of Educational Records and Testing
questions.exp: SCERT is the state-level academic body for school education.

questions.q: Which of the following is an essential feature of the project method?
options: It is a purposeful activity carried out in a natural setting
It is done under strict dictation
It avoids the use of real-life problems
questions.exp: Projects are purposeful, problem-oriented and based on real life.

questions.q: Research that focuses on testing theories without immediate application is called:
questions.exp: Basic research aims at knowledge, not an immediate solution.

questions.q: The Dalton Plan of education was proposed by:
questions.exp: Parkhurst's Dalton Plan lets pupils work at their own pace through assignments and contracts.

questions.q: A student repeatedly fails to follow the logic of loops. The best first step is to:
options: find out through questioning and a diagnostic task where the misunderstanding lies
questions.exp: Diagnosis of the specific misconception should precede any remedy.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A lesson plan should include evaluation questions.
Reason (R): Evaluation tells whether the objectives were achieved.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true and R is false
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is false and R is true
questions.exp: Evaluation is the means to know whether objectives were reached.

questions.q: An interactive whiteboard (smart board) is useful mainly because it:
options: replaces the need for lesson planning
allows the teacher to write, display digital content and save the lesson
questions.exp: It combines a touch-sensitive board with a computer and projector.

questions.q: The 'Zone of Proximal Development' (ZPD) given by Vygotsky refers to the gap between:
options: what a learner can do alone and what the learner can do with guidance
a learner's age and mental age
the teacher's and learner's knowledge of the subject
questions.exp: ZPD is the range of tasks a learner can complete only with help from a more knowledgeable person.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a core element of computational thinking?
questions.exp: The core elements are decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithm design.

questions.q: A teacher narrates how a king solved problems through logical steps to introduce algorithms to young learners. This method is:
questions.exp: Narrating a story to convey a concept or value is the storytelling method.

questions.q: In the 5+3+3+4 structure, the 'foundational stage' lasts for:
questions.exp: It includes three years of pre-school and Grades 1 and 2.

questions.q: The deductive method moves from:
questions.exp: In deduction the rule or principle is given first and then applied to particular cases.

questions.q: Inter-rater reliability concerns the:
options: agreement between different scorers marking the same answers
questions.exp: High inter-rater reliability means scorers give similar marks.

questions.q: Slow learners are usually those with an IQ in the range of about:
questions.exp: Slow learners are below average but not mentally disabled.

questions.q: Formative assessment is conducted:
options: only at the end of the year
during the learning process to improve teaching and learning
questions.exp: It gives continuous feedback, so that gaps can be corrected immediately.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes a core curriculum?
options: It is for gifted students only
It contains the subjects or experiences common to all students
It is made only by students
questions.exp: A core curriculum is the compulsory common component.

questions.q: The role of the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) is to:
options: regulate and maintain standards of teacher education
questions.exp: NCTE recognises teacher education institutions and sets norms.

questions.q: Which of the following aids requires no electricity?
questions.exp: A flip chart is paper-based and used manually.

questions.q: In the revised Bloom's taxonomy (2001), the highest level of the cognitive domain is:
questions.exp: The revised order is Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create.

questions.q: In a test, 40 out of 50 students answered an item correctly. The difficulty index (p = R/N) of this item is:
questions.exp: p = 40/50 = 0.80, so the item is easy.

questions.q: A major limitation of oral examinations is:
options: subjectivity and difficulty of keeping uniform standards
they need no preparation by the examiner
questions.exp: Different examiners and questions reduce objectivity.

questions.q: Which question type is MOST suitable to test the ability to organise and express ideas?
questions.exp: Essays test organisation, expression and integration of ideas.

questions.q: The skill of closure is mainly concerned with:
options: starting the lesson with a joke
consolidating the lesson at the end and linking it to the next
questions.exp: Closure helps students retain the main points.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the usual order in a lesson plan:
P. Presentation of content
Q. Statement of objectives
R. Evaluation
S. Introduction
questions.exp: Objectives are fixed first, followed by introduction, presentation and evaluation.

questions.q: The Academic Bank of Credit (ABC) proposed in NEP 2020 is meant to:
options: digitally store academic credits earned from different institutions
questions.exp: It facilitates credit transfer and multiple entry and exit.

questions.q: Which step of the Herbartian plan involves the teacher stating the aim of the lesson and arousing interest?
questions.exp: Preparation (introduction) states the aim and prepares the minds of learners.

questions.q: Which of the following is a good practice while using the blackboard?
options: Writing legibly and organising content in a planned layout
Standing in front of the written matter
Writing continuously without erasing or summarising
questions.exp: Legible, planned writing helps all students see and follow the content.

questions.q: The major advantage of microteaching is that it:
options: eliminates the need for school practice
is useful only for experienced teachers
provides a safe, controlled setting for practising and improving specific skills
questions.exp: Its reduced complexity lets trainees master skills before facing real classrooms.

questions.q: The best statement about teaching aids is that they:
options: are required only for weak students
should be used whether or not the topic needs them
supplement the teacher but cannot replace the teacher
questions.exp: Aids support and make teaching effective; the teacher remains central.

questions.q: The reliability coefficient normally ranges from:
questions.exp: A value near 1 indicates high reliability.

questions.q: A bulletin board in the school is mainly used to:
options: display notices, pictures and student work for information
questions.exp: It is a display aid for information and motivation.

questions.q: PM eVidya was announced to:
options: unify digital, online and on-air education initiatives
questions.exp: It brings together DIKSHA, TV channels, radio and other modes.

questions.q: The reliability of a test refers to:
options: the consistency of the test scores
questions.exp: A reliable test gives similar results on repeated administration.

questions.q: Predictive validity is established by:
options: correlating test scores with later performance
questions.exp: If scores predict future success, the test has predictive validity.

questions.q: Sharing a student's low marks with the entire class to motivate others is:
options: unethical as it violates the dignity and privacy of the student
questions.exp: Results should be communicated privately.

questions.q: Cronbach's alpha is used to estimate:
questions.exp: Alpha measures how consistently items measure the same construct.

questions.q: Corporal punishment of children in schools is prohibited by:
options: The Indian Penal Code only for adults
questions.exp: Section 17 prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment.

questions.q: Worked examples in teaching programming are effective because they:
options: show the complete solution process for learners to study
questions.exp: Studying solved examples helps beginners learn problem-solving patterns.

questions.q: A Creative Commons licence allows:
options: creators to give others permission to use their work under specified conditions
only government to use the work
questions.exp: It is a flexible copyright licensing system.

questions.q: Which of the following is an audio-visual aid?
questions.exp: A video film presents both pictures and sound.

questions.q: The main purpose of a diagnostic test is to:
options: identify the specific weaknesses of learners and their causes
questions.exp: Diagnostic testing locates learning difficulties for remediation.

questions.q:
Statement I: Formative evaluation is a continuous process.
Statement II: Summative evaluation is generally conducted at the end of a term or course.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statements I and II are false
Both Statements I and II are true
questions.exp: Formative is ongoing; summative is terminal.

questions.q: The term 'digital divide' refers to:
options: a break in a computer program
a division of the school into sections
the gap between those who have access to ICT and those who do not
the difference between two software versions
questions.exp: It describes unequal access to digital technology.

questions.q: Which of the following is a good practice for cyber safety in school?
options: Using the same simple password everywhere
Using strong passwords and not sharing them
questions.exp: Strong, private passwords protect accounts.

questions.q: An integrated curriculum is one in which:
options: subject boundaries are reduced and related content is combined around themes
each subject is taught fully separately
questions.exp: Integration links knowledge from different subjects.

questions.q: Home assignment in a lesson plan should be:
options: related to the lesson and within the capacity of students
given only to some students as punishment
questions.exp: Meaningful assignments reinforce learning.

questions.q: Dysgraphia is a learning difficulty related to:
questions.exp: Dysgraphia affects handwriting and written expression.

questions.q: Which of the following lowers the reliability of a test?
questions.exp: Ambiguity leads to inconsistent interpretation and responses.

questions.q: Presenting someone else's work as your own without acknowledgement is called:
questions.exp: Plagiarism is a violation of academic ethics.

questions.q: The principle of flexibility in curriculum means that it should:
options: be adaptable to local needs and changing times
be the same everywhere with no change
questions.exp: A flexible curriculum can be revised and adapted.

questions.q: Qualitative research mainly collects data in the form of:
questions.exp: It uses interviews, observations and documents to describe meanings.

questions.q: A good lesson plan should be:
options: flexible enough to be adjusted to the class situation
copied from another teacher without change
questions.exp: Flexibility lets the teacher respond to students' needs.

questions.q: Differentiated instruction involves:
options: giving the same task to all in the same way
adjusting content, process or product according to learner needs
questions.exp: It accommodates differences in readiness and learning style.

questions.q: Who generally conducts action research?
options: The practising teacher in his or her own class
questions.exp: Teachers research their own problems.

questions.q: Learners and teacher interact at the same time in:
questions.exp: A live virtual class is a synchronous mode.

questions.q: The 'stem' of a multiple-choice question is:
options: the question or incomplete statement presented to the learner
questions.exp: The stem poses the problem; options follow.

questions.q: A test that adequately covers the syllabus content has high:
questions.exp: Content validity is judged by how well the test represents the subject content.

questions.q: A typical microteaching lesson lasts about:
options: 5 to 10 minutes with a small group of students
40 to 45 minutes with a full class
questions.exp: Microteaching scales down time, class size and content.

questions.q: An example of hidden curriculum is:
options: students learning algebra from a textbook
students learning punctuality by watching their teacher always come on time
questions.exp: Such learning is not formally listed in any syllabus.

questions.q: Which of the following is the last step of the Herbartian plan?
questions.exp: Learners apply the generalised rule to new situations at the end.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of formative assessment?
options: A short class quiz followed by feedback
questions.exp: A short quiz with feedback helps improve learning during the course.

questions.q: The term 'action research' was first used by:
questions.exp: Kurt Lewin introduced the term in the 1940s.

questions.q: SWAYAM Prabha is:
options: a group of DTH educational channels that telecast high-quality programmes
questions.exp: It broadcasts educational content 24x7 through DTH channels.

questions.q: Grading is preferred over marking in CCE mainly because it:
options: reduces unhealthy competition and stress among students
questions.exp: Grades express performance in bands and lower the pressure of exact marks.

questions.q: A good way to teach debugging is to:
options: give students programs with errors and ask them to locate and correct them
ask them to memorise error messages
questions.exp: Learning from errors strengthens understanding.

questions.q: The best way for a teacher to handle misbehaviour is:
options: to understand its cause and respond constructively
to humiliate the student in public
questions.exp: Positive discipline addresses the cause without harming dignity.

questions.q: A podcast in education is useful mainly because it:
options: delivers audio content that learners can listen to at their convenience
questions.exp: Podcasts are portable audio learning resources.

questions.q: What should be the first step in the evaluation process?
questions.exp: Evaluation is meaningless without clearly stated objectives.

questions.q: In Herbart's five formal steps, the step that follows 'presentation' is:
questions.exp: The order is preparation, presentation, comparison (association), generalisation, application.

questions.q: In an MCQ, the incorrect options are called:
questions.exp: Distractors are plausible wrong options; the correct one is the key.

questions.q: In a symposium:
options: several speakers present different aspects of a single topic before an audience
students enact characters in a drama
a teacher dictates notes to the class
questions.exp: A symposium is a series of short prepared talks on different aspects of the same theme.

questions.q: Which of the following is a limitation of action research?
options: Findings are context-specific and cannot be easily generalised
questions.exp: The sample is usually a single class or school.

questions.q: In Dale's cone, 'verbal symbols' (spoken or written words) are placed:
options: at the top, being the most abstract
questions.exp: Words are the most abstract form of experience.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important quality of a good teacher?
questions.exp: Understanding learners together with command of the subject makes teaching effective.

questions.q: Python is often chosen as a first language in schools because it:
options: cannot be used for real applications
questions.exp: Simple syntax lets learners focus on problem-solving.

questions.q:
Statement I: Audio-visual aids can make abstract ideas easier to understand.
Statement II: Audio-visual aids should be used only at the end of a lesson.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statements I and II are true
Both Statements I and II are false
questions.exp: Aids are used wherever they help understanding, not only at the end.

questions.q:
Statement I: Teaching is always intentional and planned.
Statement II: Learning can occur incidentally, without any teacher.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statements I and II are true
Both Statements I and II are false
questions.exp: Teaching aims at specific outcomes, while learning can also happen informally and by chance.

questions.q: The national framework for the school curriculum in India is prepared by:
questions.exp: NCERT develops the National Curriculum Framework.

questions.q: A working model of a human heart is an example of:
questions.exp: Models are 3-D representations that show structure and function.

questions.q: Emotional intelligence, an idea popularised by Daniel Goleman, is the ability to:
options: recognise and manage one's own and others' emotions
questions.exp: It includes self-awareness, self-regulation and empathy.

questions.q: The major weakness of the lecture method is that:
questions.exp: The lecture method is teacher-centred and gives little scope for learner activity.

questions.q: Which of the following assessment tasks best tests the practical skills in CS?
options: Writing the definition of a compiler
Writing and running a program to solve a given problem
questions.exp: Executing a program shows application ability.

questions.q: Which of the following would INCREASE the reliability of a test?
options: Increasing the number of good-quality items
questions.exp: A longer test with well-written items gives more stable scores.

questions.q: Using praise such as 'Very good' and a nod for a correct answer is the skill of:
questions.exp: Positive verbal and non-verbal responses strengthen desired behaviour.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in curriculum development?
options: Needs assessment, objectives, content selection, learning experiences, evaluation
questions.exp: Development begins by assessing needs and defining objectives and ends with evaluation.

questions.q: Parsons problems are exercises in which students:
options: arrange scrambled lines of code in the correct order
questions.exp: They reduce the cognitive load of writing code from scratch.

questions.q: Block-based languages like Scratch are useful for beginners because they:
options: are the only way to learn programming
remove syntax errors and focus on logic
are faster than every other language
questions.exp: Drag-and-drop blocks help novices concentrate on concepts.

questions.q: A flannel board is used to:
options: present cut-out figures and symbols that stick to a cloth-covered board
questions.exp: Flannel cut-outs adhere to the cloth surface, allowing step-wise presentation.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best description of 'panel discussion'?
options: One person reads a paper without interaction
A small group of experts discusses a topic informally in front of an audience
The teacher dictates questions to the class
questions.exp: In a panel discussion the experts talk with one another under a moderator while the audience listens.

questions.q: Programmed instruction, based on Skinner's ideas, presents:
options: material in small steps with immediate feedback
questions.exp: Small steps, active response and immediate reinforcement are its features.

questions.q: Gyan Vani, in the Indian context, is:
options: a network of educational FM radio stations
questions.exp: Gyan Vani broadcasts educational radio programmes through FM stations.

questions.q: The preventive approach to classroom management emphasises:
options: planning routines and activities to avoid discipline problems
questions.exp: Good planning and engagement reduce misbehaviour.

questions.q: Which of the following is an open-source learning management system (LMS)?
questions.exp: Moodle is a widely used open-source LMS.

questions.q: Which of the following methods is MOST teacher-centred?
questions.exp: In the lecture method the teacher does most of the talking and decides everything.

questions.q: Professional ethics requires a teacher to:
options: share marks publicly to shame students
discuss students' family problems with strangers
questions.exp: Confidentiality respects the dignity and privacy of students.

questions.q: In the split-half method, the test is commonly divided into:
questions.exp: The correlation of half-scores is stepped up by the Spearman-Brown formula.

questions.q: Gagne's nine events of instruction begin with:
options: gaining the attention of the learners
questions.exp: Gaining attention is the first event, followed by informing the learner of the objective.

questions.q: While preparing PowerPoint slides for a class, which practice is NOT recommended?
options: Filling each slide with long paragraphs in small font
questions.exp: Overloaded slides reduce attention and are hard to read.

questions.q: Practicability (usability) of a test relates to:
options: ease of administration, scoring and cost
questions.exp: A test should be practical in time, cost and scoring effort.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a component of curriculum?
questions.exp: The usual components are objectives, content, learning experiences and evaluation.

questions.q: The hidden curriculum refers to:
options: the syllabus printed in the textbook
unplanned values and attitudes learnt through school life and culture
questions.exp: Hidden curriculum is learned implicitly from the school environment and teacher behaviour.

questions.q: Informed consent in educational research means that participants:
options: agree to take part after knowing the purpose and nature of the study
questions.exp: It is a basic ethical principle.

questions.q: A teacher who is always punctual and honest is serving as:
questions.exp: Students learn values by observing their teacher's conduct.

questions.q: Peer assessment means:
options: students assess each other's work using given criteria
questions.exp: Peer assessment develops critical judgement and responsibility.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Individual differences must be considered in the teaching-learning process.
Reason (R): Learners differ in ability, interest and pace of learning.
Choose the best option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Because learners differ in many respects, teaching must be adapted to them.

questions.q: The demonstration method is most suitable when:
options: students need to practise typing speed
the class has very few students
an experiment is costly or hazardous for students to perform individually
questions.exp: The teacher performs the activity while students observe, saving cost and avoiding danger.

questions.q: The parallel-forms method estimates reliability by:
options: giving two equivalent forms of the test to the same group
questions.exp: The correlation between two equivalent forms indicates reliability.

questions.q: Teaching-learning material (TLM) is listed in the lesson plan so that:
options: the aids needed are decided and arranged in advance
questions.exp: Advance planning ensures aids are available and well used.

questions.q: In a 'flipped classroom':
options: students study content at home and use class time for practice and discussion
questions.exp: Instruction is shifted outside the class so class time becomes active learning.

questions.q: Instructional objectives in a lesson plan should be written in:
questions.exp: Behavioural objectives can be checked by evaluation.

questions.q: In microteaching, a teacher trainee practises:
options: one specific teaching skill at a time
questions.exp: Focusing on a single skill makes feedback and improvement manageable.

questions.q: What is the correct order in dealing with learning difficulties?
options: Identify the problem, diagnose the cause, apply the remedy
questions.exp: A remedy is useful only after the difficulty and its cause are known.

questions.q: The satellite launched in 2004 exclusively for educational services in India is:
questions.exp: EDUSAT, launched on 20 September 2004, was dedicated to educational broadcasting.

questions.q: Which of the following verbs is NOT suitable for writing a specific measurable objective?
questions.exp: 'Appreciate' describes an internal state that cannot be directly observed.

questions.q: In Mager's ABCD format for writing objectives, 'D' stands for:
questions.exp: The ABCD elements are Audience, Behaviour, Condition and Degree.

questions.q: Review of related literature is done to:
options: know what has already been studied and avoid duplication
questions.exp: It identifies gaps and guides the design.

questions.q: NEP 2020 set a target of Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education of:
questions.exp: The aim is to raise GER to 50% by 2035.
